results.author: Oleksii Zotov
highlights:
# Automating Hetzner Cloud with the HetznerCloud .NET Library

...

###### Published

2026-09-23

...

The library splits the API into one client per resource type — `client.Servers`, `client.ServerTypes`, `client.Images`, `client.Locations`, and so on. Before we create anything, it helps to look at what we have to choose from. Paste this into `Program.cs` below the `Console.WriteLine` line.

```csharp
var serverTypes = await client.ServerTypes.GetAllAsync();
Console.WriteLine("Available server types:");
foreach (var type in serverTypes.ServerTypes.Where(t => !t.Deprecated))
{
    var price = type.Prices.FirstOrDefault(p => p.Location == "hel1");
    var monthly = price?.PriceMonthly.Net ?? 0;
    Console.WriteLine($"  {type.Name}: {type.Cores} vCPU, {type.Memory} GB RAM, " +
                      $"{type.Disk} GB {type.StorageType} - EUR {monthly.ToString("F2", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)}/mo");
}

var images = await client.Images.GetAllAsync(new ImageListOptions { Type = "system", PerPage = 20 });
Console.WriteLine("\nLatest system images:");
foreach (var image in images.Images)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"  {image.Name}: {image.Description}");
}

var locations = await client.Locations.GetAllAsync();
Console.WriteLine("\nAvailable locations:");
foreach (var location in locations.Locations)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"  {location.Name}: {location.City}, {location.Country}");
}
```

Quick rundown of what that does:

- It lists the server types that are still on sale (anything deprecated gets skipped), with their vCPU, RAM, disk, and the monthly price at the `hel1` location.
- It pulls a bunch of the newest system images — Ubuntu and friends — that you can boot a server from.
- It lists the data center locations where you'd even put your stuff.

I hard-code the `hel1` price lookup here just to keep the output tidy, and I format it with the invariant culture so it doesn't randomly switch between comma and dot depending on where you run it.

Run it:

```bash
dotnet run
```

You should get something like the listing below. The exact names and prices will change over time as Hetzner updates its catalog.

```text
Hetzner Cloud .NET Tutorial
==================================
Available server types:
  cpx##: 2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 40 GB local - EUR #.##/mo
  cpx##: 3 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 80 GB local - EUR #.##/mo
  cx##: 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 40 GB local - EUR #.##/mo
  cx##: 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 80 GB local - EUR #.##/mo
  ...

Latest system images:
  rocky-8: Rocky Linux 8
  centos-stream-9: CentOS Stream 9
  ubuntu-22.04: Ubuntu 22.04
  rocky-9: Rocky Linux 9
  ...

Available locations:
  fsn1: Falkenstein, DE
  nbg1: Nuremberg, DE
  hel1: Helsinki, FI
  ash: Ashburn, VA, US
  hil: Hillsboro, OR, US
  sin: Singapore, SG
```

One thing I learned the hard way: just because a server type shows up in the list above does not mean you can actually order it wherever you want. Some of the ARM-based types (`cpx*`, `cax*`) show a price, but the API flat-out rejects new servers for them in most locations. When we actually create a server later, I stick with `cx33`.

results.title: The Hetzner Summit 2026 is over
results.author: Adrian Macrea
highlights:
# Hetzner Summit 2026: The highlights

September 29, 2026 7 min read

...

The Hetzner Summit 2026 has ended, and we’re looking back on this successful event. It featured presentations and technical deep dives from the Hetzner and tech worlds, numerous data center tours offering exclusive behind-the-scenes insight into our technical infrastructure, various gaming and entertainment activities, and plenty of food and drinks for everyone. We showcased rack modules, multi-GPU servers, 3D printing, individual server components, and network technology—including fiber splicing. Our visitors came from all over Germany and several European countries. We planned the event entirely on our own, and over a hundred employees were involved.

...

For you, the Hetzner Summit began on Thursday, 17 September. For us, it started around a year earlier. We handled most of the planning and organization ourselves, too. An event for several hundred visitors takes a lot of preparation: we had to plan and organize the stage, technical equipment, data center tours, catering, sanitary facilities, and entertainment stations. And that was just the beginning. We made the table decorations from decommissioned graphics cards, and built the benches in front of the stage from retired Dell servers – do-it-yourself in its purest form.

...

Our guest speaker Gergely Daróczi from Spare Cores showed how Hetzner Cloud compares with other providers. He presented benchmarks and insights into the performance of different offerings.

Our second guest presentation was given by Maximilian Schilling from Warmwind. The AI startup from Jena requires a great deal of GPU performance for its applications. And that was also the focus of his talk, in which he explored the GPU dilemma Europe is facing.

...

Those who stayed in the main building could explore our various stations. At the hardware exhibition, we displayed complete rack modules just like the ones used in our data centers. These included multi-GPU racks and Custom Solutions for customers with specific requirements.

We showcased both the cooling systems and the inside of the servers, including their individual components. We manufacture some of these parts ourselves using our 3D printers, and demonstrated this live on site as well. You can read more about how we print our own server parts in this article. Visitors could also take a closer look at other server components such as RAM, SSDs, and network interface cards (NICs).
